title: Expansion Coupling

introduction.definition: An expansion (axial-float) coupling joins two shafts and lets one move axially, for example as a hot pump or turbine shaft grows. In this gear type, crowned external teeth on each hub mesh with internal teeth in a sleeve; the teeth transmit torque and can slide, and the crowning also accepts small angular and offset misalignment.
applications: Turbine- and motor-driven pumps and compressors with thermal growth
introduction.summary: An expansion (axial-float) gear coupling joins two shafts while letting one slide axially as it grows with temperature. Crowned hub teeth mesh with a sleeve's internal teeth and also accept small misalignment.

pressure.title: Teeth transmit torque and let the shaft slide
pressure.description: Torque passes from the driver hub teeth to the sleeve and on to the driven hub teeth. Because the teeth can slide axially in the sleeve, the driven shaft is free to grow with temperature (animation shows axial float) without loading the bearings, and the crowned teeth accept small angular and offset misalignment. Sliding under torque needs lubrication — gear couplings are greased or oil-fed; dry teeth wear quickly and can lock, transmitting large thrust. (Pipework "expansion couplings" are a different item.)

thrust.title: Thermal growth
thrust.description: The driven shaft grows axially; the coupling slides instead of pushing on the bearings.

video_tutorials.title: Expansion Coupling — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Expansion Coupling.
An expansion (axial-float) coupling joins two shafts and lets one move axially, for example as a hot pump or turbine shaft grows.

In this gear type, crowned external teeth on each hub mesh with internal teeth in a sleeve; the teeth transmit torque and can slide, and the crowning also accepts small angular and offset misalignment.
Typical applications include turbine- and motor-driven pumps and compressors with thermal growth; steel-mill drives and heavy machinery.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Driver Shaft & Crowned External Teeth (turning), Driven Shaft & Crowned External Teeth (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Expansion Coupling works.
The driver hub teeth turn the sleeve.
The sleeve drives the other hub.
The driven shaft grows and slides axially.
Lubricant lets the teeth slide.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Torque passes from the driver hub teeth to the sleeve and on to the driven hub teeth.
The driven shaft grows axially; the coupling slides instead of pushing on the bearings.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Expansion Coupling.
Check for grease leakage and noise.
Re-grease / check oil spray.
Inspect tooth wear; replace hubs/sleeve.
Watch for tooth wear / lock-up: rising vibration, axial thrust. Common cause: lack of lubrication, misalignment.
Watch for seal leakage: grease loss. Common cause: damaged seal.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
